subject: Food Science
title: The Microwave Oven
description: A quick, practical guide to The Microwave Oven.

hook.text: Percy Spencer discovered microwave cooking in 1945 when a chocolate bar melted in his pocket while he stood near a radar.

buildup.text: He tested popcorn kernels—they popped. Then an egg—it exploded. Spencer filed a patent and Raytheon built the first commercial.

discovery.text: Microwaves heat food by vibrating water molecules 2.45 billion times per second.

twist.text: The first microwave, the Radarange, weighed 340 kg and cost $5,000 (about $65,000 today). It was sold to restaurants.

climax.text: By 1997, 90% of US households owned a microwave. It changed cooking behavior more than any appliance.

punchline.text: A melted chocolate bar, a curious engineer, and radar technology.

quiz.question: How do microwaves heat food?
options: Using infrared radiation like an oven
By vibrating water molecules 2.45 billion times per second—friction generates heat
